ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening and enhanced due diligence for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs), heads of international organizations, and their family members and close associates, under PCMLTFA, SOR/2002-184, s 33.1, and FINTRAC client due diligence guidance. Mandatory name screening against the Global Affairs Canada automated Canadian sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; the United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 45; the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act), SC 2017, c 21; the OFAC SDN list (required for USD Swift and ACH rails); the UN Security Council Consolidated List; and applicable domestic watchlists. Screening must be performed prior to name clearance, at onboarding of any partner, prior to any capital contribution, and on an ongoing event-driven basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada online filing centre (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) for federal NUANS name pre-clearance, together with the governing provincial registry portal for the limited partnership registration (e.g., Ontario ServiceOntario Companies and Personal Property Branch, Alberta Corporate Registry, or BC Corporate Online)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A limited partnership name may be registered in English, French, or a bilingual (English-French) form. The name must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; a non-Latin original requires an official transliteration or translation into English or French. The name must include a distinctive element and a legal element denoting limited partnership status, such as 'Limited Partnership', 'Societe en commandite', 'L.P.', or 's.e.c.'. French-language naming is mandatory for records filed in Quebec. The name must not be confusingly similar to an existing corporate, partnership, or trademark name within the meaning of the CBCA ss 11-12 and applicable provincial business names legislation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS name search report is valid for 90 days for the federal name clearance and for most provincial registrations (British Columbia uses a shorter reservation window of up to 56 days for approved names). If the provincial registrar or the federal Director under CBCA s 12 rejects the proposed name, the general partner may, within 30 days of the notice of refusal, file a written appeal with the Registrar of Companies (or the Director) stating: (i) the proposed name as filed; (ii) evidence of distinctiveness, including a trademark search report and evidence of common-law use in Canada; (iii) written consent letters from any regulated body or holder of the sensitive token where the refusal is token-based; and (iv) the proposed French-language version where applicable. If the refusal is maintained, the general partner may alternatively submit a fresh NUANS search with a new proposed name and pay the applicable re-filing fee, or seek judicial review in the Federal Court (for CBCA matters) or in the superior court of the province governing the limited partnership.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is statutorily permissible as the registered office address in most provinces and for federal corporate registrations, provided the registered agent maintains a real street address in the jurisdiction for service of process. However, for a Canadian limited partnership operating a programmatic AdTech exchange and SSP platform with Swift wire and ACH payment rails, Canadian financial institutions and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) substance review require a de facto physical place of business in Canada. A pure virtual office may jeopardize banking onboarding, GST/HST registration treatment, and the pass-through eligibility of the limited partnership under Income Tax Act s 96. Recommended structure: a physical operational office in the governing province plus a registered agent's address for service of process, with books and records maintained in Canada.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk. Estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the CRA (GST/HST, income tax, or payroll audit program) or provincial registry compliance authorities for a low-risk AdTech platform is approximately 10-15%. The probability increases to 25% or higher if the limited partnership files a large GST/HST input tax credit refund, engages in non-arm's length intercompany payments, or applies for a tax clearance certificate. Transfer-pricing scrutiny under Income Tax Act s 247 is an added driver of on-site inspection in the AdTech sector.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-19 (incorporation), s. 22 (articles), s. 101 (registered office), s. 106 (by-laws), s. 125 (officers); Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512. Note: Canada has no federal limited partnership registry; the CA_FED composite is achieved via a federally incorporated general partner corporation (CBCA) and a provincial declaration under a Limited Partnerships Act (e.g., R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, s. 3 Form 1), with extra-provincial registration as required.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), Online Filing Centre; provincial registry (e.g., Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch) for the limited partnership declaration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) under the CBCA for the general partner corporation; Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership under the provincial Limited Partnerships Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a CBCA federal corporation or for a limited partnership; the GP may be incorporated with nil paid-up capital and shares without par value. No escrow account is required for this ordinary formation; CBCA s. 47 escrow rules apply only to controlled acquisitions of certain late-stage resource companies. Initial LP capital contributions are contractual and set by the limited partnership agreement, not prescribed by statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation adopt and maintain its registered office at [registered office address in Ontario], and that [Name] be appointed to manage the registration of the office address with Corporations Canada. RESOLVED THAT the Corporation subscribe for and accept the issuance of 100 common shares in its authorized capital for the digital advertising exchange business described in the Articles. RESOLVED THAT the Corporation, as general partner of the limited partnership, shall file the limited partnership declaration and extra-provincial registrations. RESOLVED THAT [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Treasurer, and [Name] Secretary, with full authority to execute filings, open bank accounts, and sign contracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada via accredited NUANS service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) to confirm that the proposed federal corporate name for the general partner (e.g., '[GP Name] Inc.') is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing trademarks or corporate names. Optionally reserve the approved name for up to 90 days. Ensure the GP name does not contain designating words implying limited partnership status (e.g., 'Limited' or 'LP'). The LP name itself must contain the word 'Limited' or 'Ltee'.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with designating words (Inc., Corp., Ltd.)
Statement of business activity (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810, programmatic ad exchange)
List of shareholders and directors for conflict-of-interest review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion, file a new NUANS search with a revised distinctive element, obtain a written consent from the conflicting name holder, or request departmental review by Corporations Canada under subsection 12(2) of the CBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Incorporation of the General Partner Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, ISED, Online Filing Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001 (Articles of Incorporation) electronically through the Corporations Canada portal. Provide the NUANS report, a registered office address in Canada, a minimum of one director (at least 25% resident Canadian directors unless an exemption applies), and one or more classes of shares. Pay the C$200 online filing fee. Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the GP receives its federal corporate identification number. The GP may then adopt by-laws and execute the limited partnership declaration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are rejected for non-compliance, correct the deficiencies and re-file online. For typographical errors in the issued certificate, apply for a certificate of amendment or a corrected certificate under subsection 264(1) of the CBCA within 30 days of the certificate date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial companies registry (e.g., Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership in the province where the LP will have its head office. The declaration must state the LP's name (including 'Limited' or 'Ltee'), the registered office address, the full legal name and address of the general partner (the newly incorporated federal CBCA corporation), and a statement that the GP is authorized to act on the LP's behalf. Pay the provincial registration fee. The filing perfects the limited liability shield for limited partners.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the GP's Certificate of Incorporation
Limited partnership agreement (reference copy for internal records)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried, verify the GP name and office address, then file an amended Form 1 or a supplementary declaration. Late-filing penalty relief may be sought under provincial rules if the declaration is regularized promptly after the omission is discovered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Extra-Provincial Registration and Bank Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Extra-provincial registries in each province where the entity carries on business (e.g., Ontario under the Extra-Provincial Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.27)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the LP and GP 'carry on business' in other provinces. If so, file the applicable extra-provincial registration form and obtain a licence of extra-provincial registration in each such province. Thereafter, open a business bank account in the LP's name: present the GP's certificate, the LP declaration, an excerpt of the First Board Resolution appointing signing officers, and complete the bank's KYC/AML forms, including intended payment rails (SWIFT wire and ACH Direct).
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the federal certificate and articles
Certified copy of the LP declaration
Banking resolution from the First Board Resolution
Beneficial ownership and KYC declarations for bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the extra-provincial registration is rejected or a compliance order is issued, regularize the deficiency by re-filing with corrected information and pay the applicable late fee. If a bank queries the beneficial ownership, provide a revised organizational chart and certified registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN) for the limited partnership through BRO, using the GP's federal corporate identifier where applicable. Register for GST/HST under section 240 of the Excise Tax Act if taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 annually (or voluntarily). Register for payroll deductions if employees will be hired, and for corporate income tax with respect to the GP's taxable income. Maintain the LP's T5013 Partnership Information Return filing correspondence and details of cumulative eligible capital. Confirm that the LP is treated as a pass-through entity and that the GP's CBCA corporate registration does not disturb the partnership classification under the Income Tax Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation of the GP
Estimated annual revenue and payroll data
Partnership agreement for tax allocation rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN is not activated or accounts are misclassified, contact the CRA Business Window or file Form RC1A to amend registration. Retroactive GST/HST registration may be requested under subsection 242(1) of the Excise Tax Act for the prior month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records, By-laws, and Annual Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate secretary of the GP; Corporations Canada annual return system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate minute book: adopt By-law Number 1 (governance), issue share certificates to the founding shareholder(s) of the GP, and record the First Board Resolution. File the annual return with Corporations Canada within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation, and renew the provincial LP registration annually where required. Maintain the LP's register of limited partners and capital account ledgers in Canada. Ensure that the registered office is properly signposted and that statutory records are accessible for inspection.
required_dossiers: LP capital account ledgers and limited partner register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return lapses, file it immediately with the applicable late fee; if dissolution has occurred, apply for reinstatement under subsection 212(1) of the CBCA within three years of dissolution. For provincial LP lapses, file a reinstatement and notice of change with the provincial registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 (programmatic ad exchange, DSP/SSP platform) is a non-industrial digital activity. Sectoral oversight rests with the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) for electronic marketing and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC) for PIPEDA compliance. No federal industrial licensing board authorizes this activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None mandatory. Optional validations: IAB Canada membership and adherence to the Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada (DAAC) self-regulatory principles; registration as a data processor under Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector if processing in Quebec.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC); Impact Assessment Agency of Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is an information services business with no physical works listed under the Physical Activities Regulations (SOR/2019-285) made under the Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28, s. 1. No EIA registration or full report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None for wastewater or VOC discharges since no manufacturing facility is present. If the company operates on-premises data servers, comply with: federal GHG reporting threshold (50 kt CO2e/year) under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program; provincial e-waste manifests (e.g., Ontario Regulation 103/04); and CRTC content-neutral network requirements. Digital-only operations are otherwise subject to general municipal stormwater and solid waste bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the National Fire Code of Canada 2020 and local fire marshal inspection for any office premises; municipal occupancy permit issued by the local building department; workers' compensation registration (e.g., WSIB in Ontario) for any employees; compliance with Canada Labour Code, Part II (occupational health and safety) for federally regulated workers; structural load inspection only if on-premises server racks are installed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); digital portal: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO); customs counterpart: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) through the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian limited partnership obtains a 9-digit Business Number (BN), which is the federal tax identifier and the base for all program accounts. Application is made by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) via BRO or by paper, or through Form GST20 for non-resident simplified GST/HST registration where applicable. Required particulars for the LP include: executed limited partnership agreement; legal name and date of formation; each general partner's SIN, BN, or foreign tax identifier; the Canadian agent's physical address for service; and a description of the ISIC 7310 programmatic advertising and SSP activities. Upon issuance, the CRA assigns program accounts with two-letter suffixes and a four-digit account number, e.g., RT for GST/HST, RM for import/export, RP for payroll, and RC where a corporate general partner is separately registered. The same BN is used for the T5013 partnership information return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - a Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax purposes: the LP computes income and loss at the partnership level under ITA section 96, but no Part I tax is levied on the partnership itself; each partner is separately liable on their share of income. Limited partners enjoy liability limited to contributed capital and unpaid commitments. For GST/HST purposes, however, the partnership is a separate 'person' and is the registrant (ETA section 272.1), distinct from the partners. Territorial scope: a Canadian-resident partnership is taxed worldwide through its partners; non-resident partners deriving Canadian business income through the LP are taxed on a net basis under Part I, with no Part XIII withholding on ordinary business allocations, provided timely returns are filed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic 'check-the-box' election; entity classification follows strict legal form. Available elections material to a Canadian LP include: (i) ITA section 249.1(4) election to adopt a non-calendar partnership fiscal period; (ii) ITA section 216 election by a non-resident partner to be taxed on a net Part I basis for Canadian rental or timber royalty income instead of Part XIII gross withholding; (iii) ITA section 150(2) election to file a partnership information return where not otherwise mandatory; (iv) ETA section 177 agency/principal election to fix which party is the supplier of advertising services for GST/HST; and (v) for hybrid mismatch arrangements, compliance with ITA sections 18.4 to 18.6 (effective for arrangements entered into or substantially modified after the applicable 2022 implementation date) through documented commercial substance. A foreign partner's home-jurisdiction classification election (e.g., U.S. check-the-box) does not alter Canadian domestic classification of the LP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) plus Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) in participating provinces; the CA_FED scope applies to the headline federal GST of 5%; Quebec additionally imposes QST at 9.975%, and British Columbia, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba operate separate provincial RST/PST regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the small supplier threshold; registration becomes mandatory in the calendar quarter in which the LP's taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 either in that single quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. A non-resident LP supplying specified digital goods or services to Canadian consumers is subject to the same CAD 30,000 threshold under the simplified GST/HST regime; once registration becomes obligatory, the registrant must remain registered even if revenue subsequently falls below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no government-operated digital stamping, and no mandatory API-based clearance loop exists in Canada. GST/HST registrants must issue invoices satisfying ETA section 221(2), containing the supplier's BN and GST/HST account number, the recipient's name, the date, a description of the supply, the consideration, and the tax amount. Electronic invoices and books are valid if maintained in a readable, printable, and accessible format at a CRA-accessible location (ETA section 286; CRA Electronic Records policy). PEPPOL-based e-invoicing is voluntary in Canada; there is no mandatory fiscal-data interchange with CRA for B2B invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for services, including programmatic ad-exchange, DSP/SSP connectivity, and digital ad-placement services, is available under Part V of Schedule VI to the ETA when the Canadian LP supplies the service to a non-resident recipient who is not registered for GST/HST and who is not present in Canada at the time of supply (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, section 7). The supply is not zero-rated if it relates to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or a service performed while the recipient is physically present in Canada. The residence of the commercial recipient (the non-resident DSP, agency, or advertiser) governs for B2B supplies; the fact that an advertisement may target Canadian audiences does not, by itself, defeat zero-rating. Physical goods exported by the LP, if any, are zero-rated under sections 5 and 6 of Part V, Schedule VI, subject to CBSA export reporting. Input tax credits on Canadian overhead attributable to zero-rated exports are recoverable through the LP's ordinary GST/HST return; refunds are subject to CRA proof of export and records audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Export Declaration / e-Export report filed through CARM (required only if physical goods are exported; pure digital advertising services require no customs declaration)

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical media or ad-tech hardware (servers, terminals); for pure services, retain the executed DSP/SSP service agreement, insertion orders, and dated technical service logs

Inward Remittance Certificate equivalent - SWIFT MT103 or ACH bank confirmation evidencing remittance of export proceeds from the non-resident DSP counterpart, together with the contract, invoices, and a certification of the recipient's non-resident status (e.g., certificate of residency or foreign incorporation document)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated export and claw back unremitted GST/HST plus associated input tax credits within 4 years of the applicable assessment date (ETA section 298), extended to 7 years for negligence or misrepresentation, and without limitation for fraud. If zero-rating is denied, the LP must remit 5% GST on the full supply value plus interest at prescribed rates, and may be liable under ETA section 285 for false statements or omissions to the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the unreported tax. Failure to collect or remit tax attracts penalties under ETA section 280, and deliberate evasion is indictable under ETA section 327 and ITA section 239, with fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment of up to 5 years. Canada does not impose a statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is an internal compliance control, and significant delay in remittance of export proceeds may trigger CRA scrutiny of the transaction's authenticity, potential application of the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA section 245), and evidentiary challenges to the zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority and regulator of retail payment service providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act (S.C. 2021, c. 23, supervisory regime in force November 2024). Foreign exchange administration is shared: the Department of Finance Canada holds statutory powers under the Currency Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. C-52) and the Bretton Woods Agreements Act, while FINTRAC administers cross-border funds reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA, S.C. 2000, c. 17).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account; Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and applies a free-floating CAD exchange rate with no capital-control licensing, no profit-remittance permit, and no conversion approval for partnership distributions. Profit remittance note: allocations of Canadian-source partnership income to non-resident partners may be subject to Part XIII withholding under the Income Tax Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. 1, 5th Supp.) at 25% unless a tax treaty reduces the rate; distributions characterized as return of capital are generally non-taxable. An NR6 undertaking with matching T5013 reporting should be established in the bank's cash management profile to avoid trapped withholding on a US LP/LLC partner structure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender ratio and no mandatory conversion applies in Canada. Export and ad-tech service proceeds may be retained in USD or any convertible currency. Mandatory administrative obligations: cross-border electronic funds transfers equal to or exceeding CAD $10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC within 5 business days, and physical transportation of currency or monetary instruments equal to or exceeding CAD $10,000 must be declared at the border under the Cross-Border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reporting Regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD sub-ledger Operational Account with BMO Harris correspondent

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Canada has no 'EMI' licence equivalent to the EEA. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) offering CAD wallets must register as Money Services Businesses with FINTRAC under PCMLTFA and, for payment services to Canadian users, register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act. Legal constraint: an unregistered offshore EMI servicing a Canadian entity would breach RPAA obligations and FINTRAC registration under PCMLTFA s. 11, and deposits would not be CDIC-insured. Recommended use: collect-only virtual IBAN for low-value SSP receivables, with weekly sweeps to the Schedule I operating account; do not use an offshore EMI as the primary clearing or disbursement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote and video-based onboarding is permissible under FINTRAC's non-face-to-face verification rules if dual-source identification is applied, but most Schedule I banks require a live video or physical interview with the signing officers of the General Partner before the AML committee approves an LP account. A physical Canada visit by the GP's authorized signatory is strongly recommended to negotiate the banking agreement and evidence operational substance. The bank will require disclosure of all limited partners holding 25% or more beneficial ownership under FINTRAC guidance; a W-8BEN-E or W-9 identity pack is required for each US-domiciled partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: limited partnership interests held through a US LLC/LP chain where a natural person is not immediately identifiable on provincial registry extracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified limited partnership agreement and provincial certificate of limited partnership; organizational chart showing look-through attribution to natural persons; Canadian counsel legal opinion on PCMLTFA ownership attribution; FINTRAC ownership schedule; sworn declaration from the General Partner confirming no undisclosed principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident founder capital injection arriving from personal or officer-level accounts inconsistent with the LP's name, triggering a source-of-funds investigation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital contribution schedule cross-referenced to the LP agreement; 3 months of funding bank statements; tax clearance records; apostilled corporate resolutions; letter of explanation; 30-60 day seasoning of the capital escrow account before any operational disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Programmatic ad exchange receipts from DSP/SSP counterparties flagged as opaque third-party payments, engaging an ad-fraud or trade-based money-laundering typology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements with named ad platforms; IAB or Media Rating Council membership evidence; transaction-level reconciliation exports from the ad server; SOC 2 Type II report; segregated client collection account; documented wallet-to-bank traffic flow diagram for the AML officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP name-match hits on passive limited partners due to common-name coincidences or US 50% ownership exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership register with OFAC, EU, and UN sanctions screening certificates; sanctions-risk rationale memo from the designated AML officer; evidence of passive limited partner status under applicable Canadian limited partnership law; written undertaking to provide ongoing monitoring alerts to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: USD capital injections: remit via Fedwire or CHIPS to the Canadian bank's US correspondent (e.g., RBC US, BMO Harris, TD Bank US), then internal transfer to the LP's CAD or USD account at the Canadian Schedule I bank. Domestic CAD legs: settle real-time via Lynx, Payments Canada's large-value system, using SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pain.001. Required wire content: MT103 Field 50K (remitter), Field 57A (beneficiary bank transit and SWIFT BIC), Field 70 must state 'Capital contribution - LP agreement dated [date], clause [x]', and Field 72 for any reference to the escrow account. Compliance protocol: report any cross-border EFT of CAD $10,000 or more to FINTRAC within 5 business days; confirm no sanctions hits at the US correspondent; hold funds in the Capital Escrow Account for 30-60 days while the bank completes source-of-funds verification; maintain a capital-call ledger indexed to the provincial LP register. Purpose-code note: Canada does not maintain a restrictive purpose-code table, but the narrative should use 'Equity capital contribution - software services platform' to steer the bank's reporting classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (a) domestic CAD recurring vendor and DSP settlement payments via Payments Canada ACSS through ACH credit (target rail: ACH_Direct), batch T+1; (b) domestic CAD high-value and time-critical disbursements via Lynx using SWIFT MT103 (target rail: Swift_Wire); (c) cross-border USD trade settlements via SWIFT MT103 through the bank's US correspondent, with ISO 20022 pain.001 advice; (d) commercial documentary credits issued subject to UCP 600 (ICC Publication 600) and standby letters of credit for hosting and data-center agreements. Payment control: every disbursement must pass a three-way match of invoice, executed contract, and traffic reconciliation report from the ad exchange platform. Canadian clearing is consolidated under Payments Canada with OSFI-regulated banks as the only direct participants; the LP therefore executes all rails through its deposit bank, not as a direct participant.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD outright forwards with a Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, supported by a credit support annex
CAD/USD FX swaps (principal and interest exchange) for liquidity rebalancing between USD revenue receipts and CAD operating expenses
Cross-currency basis swaps converting USD-denominated ad-tech revenue streams into CAD liabilities for matched funding
Purchased CAD/USD vanilla options or zero-premium collars to cap adverse FX moves on downside revenue protection

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): legally permissible but commercially unnecessary for CAD given deep deliverable markets; available only for cross-currency exposures to inconvertible EM currencies through the Canadian bank's offshore desk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return, including T5013SUM and partner slips where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500 plus a penalty up to CAD 7,500 for missing or false partner information; continued non-compliance can trigger CRA audits, reassessments, and partner-level penalties. CRA does not administratively strike off partnerships.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return where the limited partnership is a GST/HST registrant using the annual filing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the deadline is March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 1% of unremitted GST/HST increasing after four months, plus daily compound interest of 6% per annum; repeated non-compliance may lead to prosecution and revocation of GST/HST registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provincial limited partnership annual declaration or renewal, where the partnership is registered in a provincial jurisdiction; no Canada-wide federal limited partnership registry exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Applicable provincial registry, including Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, British Columbia Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, or Registraire des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; generally due within 60 to 90 days after the registration anniversary or the provincial filing month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties plus risk of administrative cancellation of limited partnership registration; cancellation may expose limited partners to general partner liability for obligations incurred after the registration is struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporations Canada annual return, if the general partner of the limited partnership is a federal CBCA corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director under the Canada Business Corporations Act, Corporations Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of the federal corporation's incorporation or continuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for one year may cause the Director to dissolve the corporation; after dissolution, corporate property may escheat to the Crown and directors may lose the ability to enforce corporate contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML and beneficial-ownership record-keeping cycle for a low-risk reporting entity under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing obligation; reportable transactions generally must be reported within 15 days after the transaction, with no annual FINTRAC return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for serious non-compliance; FINTRAC does not administratively strike off partnerships or corporations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No standalone federal statutory audit is imposed on a limited partnership. A mandatory independent audit is triggered when the partnership is a reporting issuer, is an investment fund distributing under a prospectus exemption, is required by its partnership agreement or lender, or when the corporate general partner is a CBCA offering corporation. Otherwise, the partners may elect a review engagement or prepare financial statements under private enterprise standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises for private partnerships; tax-basis statements are not acceptable for statutory reporting purposes under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership of the limited partnership must be confirmed at the start of any business relationship and updated when there is a change in the general or limited partners, or when a risk-relevant change occurs under PCMLTFA. There is no separate federal UBO annual filing for limited partnerships; provincial registries may require beneficial ownership declarations with the annual declaration. If a CBCA corporation is the general partner, Corporations Canada requires the corporation to maintain an Individuals with Significant Control register and confirm it in the corporation's annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General and Limited Partners
Register of Transfers of Limited Partnership Interests
Register of Individuals with Significant Control, where the general partner is a CBCA corporation
Minute Book and Partner Consent Resolutions
General Ledger, Accounts Receivable and Payable Subsidiary Ledgers, and Source Documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - USD 2,500 per year for a Canadian registered office and corporate agent, including provincial extra-provincial registration services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 30,000 per year for a compact AdTech limited partnership, depending on consolidated revenue, number of partners, and group timing requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (federal general corporate tax rate after 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction; the limited partnership is fiscally transparent and Canadian-source income is taxed in the hands of its partners rather than at the LP level)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No provincial or federal tax holiday applies to ad-tech platform income. Preferential deductions and credits include SR&ED investment tax credits (up to 35% refundable for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations, otherwise 15% non-refundable), accelerated capital cost allowance for computer hardware and data infrastructure, immediate expensing for certain Canadian-manufactured assets, and CRA-recognized deductions for advertising and data acquisition if reasonably incurred and documented.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T5013 Partnership Information Return plus corresponding T5013 slips; filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency's T5013 Internet Filing service or commercially accepted EFILE software. Paper filing is available for certain small partnerships but e-filing is mandatory for returns with 50 or more information slips.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the partnership's fiscal period; a calendar-year fiscal period is required unless a CRA-approved alternate fiscal period has been elected. No quarterly instalment return is required solely from the LP, but partners pay instalments on their allocated Canadian-source income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period. A December 31 year-end would require filing by no later than May 31 of the following calendar year unless the date falls on a weekend or statutory holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross programmatic advertising revenue from real-time ad exchange, demand-side platform (DSP), supply-side platform (SSP), and audience data services. Include bid settlement fees, exchange commissions, data management fees, and related service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source revenue attributable to the non-resident partner's Canadian permanent establishment. Amounts received for services wholly provided outside Canada are sourced according to sections 115 and 104 of the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Cost of Ad Inventory and Technology Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List costs for third-party publisher inventory, data licensing, cloud-hosting infrastructure, measurement software, and programmatic bidding technology. Deductibility is limited by the reasonableness requirement in section 67 of the Income Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs allocated to a non-resident partner must comply with section 247 transfer pricing rules and be supported by contemporaneous documentation. Excessive management, royalty, or intra-group fees are disallowed unless arm's length pricing is proven.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Partner Allocation of Net Income/Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate the partnership's Canadian-source income or loss between the general partner and limited partners pursuant to the limited partnership agreement. Schedule 50 or the equivalent schedule must show the exact percentage and amount allocated to each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporate partners, the allocated share is subject to Part I tax and potentially the 25% branch tax under section 219 if the corporate partner carries on business in Canada through a permanent establishment. Treaty residence and LOB requirements must be met to claim relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose each transaction between the partnership and a non-arm's length non-resident person, including bid-streaming fees, intercompany SSP platform access, and intangibles licensing. Provide country of residence and aggregate dollar value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner must identify every controlled transaction with the Canadian LP and provide the T5013 counterparties' tax identification numbers. Failure to characterize the arrangement correctly may invoke section 247 penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013 attracts a penalty of CAD 25 per partner per month, up to a maximum of 12 months, plus an administrative penalty of CAD 100 under subsection 162(7) for failure to file an information return. Prescribed interest and an additional 3% daily compound surcharge accrue on any unpaid federal tax. Gross negligence can result in a penalty equal to 50% of the understated amount under subsection 163(2), and criminal prosecution carries fines from 50% to 200% of the evaded tax plus imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII for Canadian-source dividends paid to non-resident persons. For the Canadian limited partnership, ordinary profit distributions are not dividends and do not trigger Part XIII dividend withholding; rather, non-resident partners are subject to Part I tax on their allocated Canadian-source income and, for corporate partners, the 25% branch tax under Part XIV may apply to unremitted after-tax earnings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident seeking a reduced rate under a Canada income tax treaty must provide the Canadian withholding agent with CRA Form NR301 (Declaration of Entitlement to Treaty Benefits) and a valid Certificate of Residence issued by the treaty state's competent authority before payment is processed. CRA may also require a Form NR7 application for refund if excessive withholding has already occurred; all supporting documentation, including financial statements and ownership disclosure, must be retained for CRA audit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for royalty and interest paid to non-residents. Domestic law exempts certain arm's-length interest. Applicable treaty rates vary: interest typically 0% to 15%, royalties typically 10% to 15%; under the Canada-US treaty, ordinary arm's-length interest can be exempt and most software/copyright royalties are capped at 10% when the beneficial owner meets the limitation-on-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No explicit statutory threshold creates a personal filing trigger for a standalone Master File/Local File in Canada. Under subsection 247(4), contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be prepared and maintained when the aggregate amount of controlled transactions involving non-arm's length non-residents exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in a fiscal year. Consolidated groups with revenue of at least CAD 2,500,000,000 in a preceding year are subject to Country-by-Country reporting and are expected to maintain OECD-aligned Master File and Local File documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate a territorial Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to offshore financial centres. Substance requirements are imposed through the general anti-avoidance rule in section 245, the sham doctrine, and the OECD permanent establishment tests. An AdTech LP claiming Canadian treaty benefits or deducting intra-group expenses must maintain real decision-making, actual employees, office presence, server assets, risk-bearing capacity, and substantive commercial contracts in Canada. Artificial interposition between Canadian advertisers and foreign publishers will be disregarded and reassessed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating gross programmatic bid revenue, creating fictitious publisher invoices to inflate costs, routing Canadian ad exchange fees through shell entities, or failing to report the Canadian-source income allocated to a non-resident partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil reassessment with back taxes and compounded interest; gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated amount under subsection 163(2). Criminal prosecution under section 239 of the Income Tax Act exposes penalties ranging from 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment for up to five years. CRA can also obtain jeopardy orders freezing bank accounts and pending assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner and managers who authorize false filings or diversion schemes can be held personally liable under joint and several liability. Civil restitution, confiscation orders, pre-trial travel restrictions, restraint orders, and imprisonment are all available. The corporate veil is pierced where a limited partner participates in control or where the entity is a total sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length fees to a foreign related SSP or DSP entity, using a cost-plus margin outside the arm's length range, failing to prepare contemporaneous documentation for controlled transactions above CAD 1,000,000, or shifting Canadian AdTech profits through intangibles to a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust the transfer price to the arm's length result under subsection 247(2), deny deduction for excessive payments, and charge interest on the reassessed amount. A gross benefit adjustment also triggers a penalty of 10% of the net upward adjustment where reasonable efforts have not been made. Country-by-Country non-compliance can result in additional audit consequences and administrative penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation or sign corporate tax returns containing inflated deductions can be assessed for civil penalties if they knowingly participated. The limited partner veil can be pierced for active participation in the mispricing; extreme cases expose directors to regulatory investigation and criminal liability for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and General Anti-Avoidance Rule
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Canadian limited partnership as a conduit shell with no active ad operations, engaging in treaty-shopping between Canada and a third-country parent, interposing a foreign holding company to avoid Canadian branch tax, or executing circular financing transactions that lack commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The GAAR permits CRA to deny the resulting tax benefit, reassess partners at applicable Part I and Part XIII rates, impose interest, and apply gross negligence penalties. CRA may also disregard the existence of the shell and treat the foreign parent as directly carrying on business in Canada. Withholding obligations may be re-characterized and assessed against the Canadian payer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the LP's general partner may be personally liable for unremitted withholding tax under subsection 227.1 where the entity is stripped of assets. Civil avoidance remedies and fraudulent conveyance actions can remove the protection of limited liability. Senior managers involved in a sham arrangement are exposed to criminal prosecution, bail restrictions including travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating unregistered money-service-business activities by settling programmatic advertising payments on behalf of third-party advertisers and publishers, or failing to register as a money services business with FINTRAC when the LP engages in funds transfer, foreign exchange, or virtual currency settlement without exemptions. Also, failing to report large periodic payment transactions or suspicious transactions related to ad trafficking and money mule schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation are routinely issued to non-registered payment intermediaries. Criminal prosecution for money laundering under the Criminal Code, specifically section 462.31, carries imprisonment up to 10 years and fines at the court's discretion. Asset forfeiture orders can attach profits from unlawful transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers, directors, and partners who knowingly allow unregistered money laundering activity lose limited-liability protection and can be individually prosecuted. Sanctions can include civil restitution, surrender of passports and travel bans as bail conditions, seizure of personal assets, and imprisonment. Compliance officers and directors are personally accountable for failure to file Suspicious Transaction Reports where knowledge can be established.
